brief: A workbench organizer: two storeys, bins on top, a drawer below, all edges capped.

requirements.evidence: Level 0 (ground) has full bases at (0,0),(1,0),(0,1) plus a notch drawer frame at (1,1,0); level 1 has full bases at (0,0),(1,0),(0,1) carrying bins.
Three hex-bin-full-div3 (3-compartment full-depth) bins at level 1 cells (0,0,1), (1,0,1), (0,1,1).

Notch drawer frame (hex-drawer-frame-notch-mf) at (1,1,0) on storey 0. The configurator offered no separate drawer part; the frame is the only drawer unit placed, and I did not confirm a pull-out drawer body sits inside it.
capOpenFaces added 17 solid end caps on every open face; lockJoints added 3 joint bolts. check_build: ok, meshClash clear, no issues.

finish.summary: Built a two-storey organizer: a 3-cell ground storey with a notch drawer frame, and a 3-cell upper storey with three 3-compartment bins. All open faces are capped and joints locked; check_build reports ok with meshClash clear. Not dressed with props, since the brief is about structure. The drawer is the weakest point: only the drawer frame is placed, and I could not confirm a drawer body inside it.

lines.label: Edge cap · male, two stories tall
M3 x 10 socket head screw, ISO 4762
M6 x 20 socket head screw, ISO 4762
M6 x 25 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.
